thread.title: Humana expects to win back just over 40% of the members hit by its 2027 Medicare Advantage plan exits - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Humana expects to win back just over 40% of the members hit by its 2027 Medicare Advantage plan exits - NewsBreak

author: Elizabeth Blessing
title: Humana expects to win back just over 40% of the members hit by its 2027 Medicare Advantage plan exits - NewsBreak
text:
By Elizabeth Blessing ,
21 hours ago
Humana told investors on its July 29 earnings call that the Medicare Advantage plans it is exiting for 2027 will affect roughly 600,000 members, and that the company expects to win back just over 40 percent of them. The finance chief said the recapture figure is not a guess pulled from nowhere: it matches almost exactly what happened the last time Humana dropped a round of plans, in 2025. For everyone else caught in the exits, the number previews how much competition for their business is coming once the enrollment season opens this fall.
What Humana Told Its Investors on July 29 The disclosure came during Humana’s second-quarter 2026 earnings call, in a transcript the company posted through its own investor relations site . Chief Financial Officer Celeste Mellet told analysts, “For 2027, we anticipate these plan exits will impact approximately 600,000 members, though we will work to recapture a significant portion of that volume as we did in 2025.” The comment arrived as routine financial guidance, the kind of detail insurers walk investors through every year as they finalize which Medicare Advantage plans they will keep selling, and in which counties, for the coming plan year.
President and Chief Executive Officer James Rechtin used the same call to tie the 2027 bid decisions to a longer financial target, saying the approach was meant to keep Humana “on track to deliver our 2028 commitment of returning to a sustainable margin of at least 3%.” Plan exits, in that framing, are one lever in a multi-year financial plan rather than a standalone decision about any single market.
What a plan-ending notice leaves out: A letter announcing that a 2027 Medicare Advantage plan is being discontinued explains that coverage is ending, not how the replacement Humana is offering compares with every other plan selling in the same county, a comparison built into The 2027 Medicare Open Enrollment Decision Kit .
The Just-Over-40% Recapture Rate, Explained Recapture is the industry’s term for what happens when a member whose plan disappears ends up choosing a different plan from the same company instead of leaving for a competitor. Mellet’s forecast for 2027 leaned directly on that history: “we expect to capture a similar portion as we did in 2025. If you remember, it was just over 40%,” she told analysts. That means Humana is telling its own investors that roughly three in five of the 600,000 affected members are expected to land somewhere else, whether with a different insurer or in Original Medicare, once their current Humana plan stops existing for 2027.
Humana has not published a county-by-county list of which specific plans are being discontinued, and no member learns an individual status from an earnings call. Anyone whose plan is exiting will find out the way Medicare Advantage members always do: through a formal notice mailed by the plan, arriving in the fall ahead of the change taking effect.
That decision, for every one of the 600,000 members involved, has to happen inside a fixed calendar window. A federal enrollment-periods fact sheet sets the fall Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 through December 7, with any change taking effect January 1, the same roughly eight-week stretch in which a recaptured member re-enrolls with Humana and everyone else picks something new.
A Margin Target Behind the Strategy The exits are not happening in isolation from the rest of Humana’s finances. Rechtin’s comments tied the 2027 bidding strategy directly to the company’s 2028 margin goal, a signal that a plan’s profitability, not just its enrollment size, is what determines whether it survives into the next plan year. That framing matters for anyone trying to guess whether a favorite local plan is at risk: a plan can be popular in its market and still get dropped if its underlying economics no longer fit what the company needs across its whole book of business.
Federal payment policy adds another layer to that math. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services finalized a 2.48 percent average increase in what it pays Medicare Advantage plans for 2027, or more than $13 billion industrywide, according to the agency’s own rate-announcement fact sheet . CMS also disclosed that once projected growth in enrollee risk scores is factored in, the effective increase reaches 4.98 percent, a detail insurers weigh alongside their own cost trends when deciding which plans still pencil out.
How 2025’s Exits Compare Humana shed roughly 500,000 members when it trimmed its Medicare Advantage lineup for 2025, according to Becker’s Payer’s review of the company’s disclosures , a smaller number than the roughly 600,000 facing exits for 2027. If the 2027 recapture rate lands where Mellet described, at just over 40 percent, close to 240,000 of the affected members would end up in a different Humana plan, leaving the remaining majority to either switch insurers or move to Original Medicare.
A Wider Pullback Across Medicare Advantage Humana is not the only insurer pulling back from the business. The same Becker’s Payer review reported that UnitedHealthcare’s Medicare Advantage membership fell roughly 9 percent in 2026 and Elevance Health’s dropped 14 percent, even as Humana’s own footprint contracted to 46 states and about 85 percent of U.S. counties, down from 89 percent previously. The pattern across three of the industry’s largest insurers suggests the pressure behind Humana’s 2027 exits is an industrywide response to rising medical costs and tighter federal payments, not a problem specific to one company.
What Losing a Medicare Advantage Plan Can Change When a Medicare Advantage plan is discontinued, a member loses more than an insurance ID card. Supplemental extras that came bundled with the plan, dental cleanings, vision exams, hearing aid allowances or an over-the-counter allowance, can disappear too if the replacement plan does not carry the same package. Humana’s earnings call did not detail which specific benefits are attached to the plans being dropped, but the framing on the call makes clear the decision was driven by the company’s own financial targets, not by any individual member’s medical needs.
summary: Humana told investors on its July 29 earnings call that the Medicare Advantage plans it is exiting for 2027 will affect roughly 600,000 members, and that the company expects to win back just over 40 percent of them. A federal enrollment-periods fact sheet sets the fall Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 through December 7, with any change taking effect January 1, the same roughly eight-week stretch in which a recaptured member re-enrolls with Humana and everyone else picks something new.
